reasons: Claimed status is 'compliant' and the finding correctly leaves the text unmodified with no counterparty comment, which is the expected output for a compliant classification.

The cited text supports the fallback position: the minimum monthly floor in Section 5(a) is confined to the current 1-year term (Section 13, auto-renewal with 30 days' non-renewal notice) and Section 14 provides a convenience termination that ends the minimum roughly 30-60 days after notice, so the commitment is reducible on notice.

No shortfall payment, penalty or acceleration mechanic appears in the cited paragraphs, so there is no take-or-pay penalty and the clause is not in walk-away territory (multi-year take-or-pay with no exit).

Minor sub-elements short of preferred wording (non-contestable minimums under Section 6, blank dollar amounts, and the Section 4/5 mis-cross-reference and 'Subject to Section 4' ambiguity) are appropriately noted in the rationale rather than redlined, per the classification semantics.
